generation.explanation: Think of x² + 6x as an area. x² is an x-by-x square, and 6x is a strip of width 6 and length x. Cut that strip in half and put one 3-by-x piece on the right of the square and the other along the bottom. Now the shape is almost a square with side x + 3. Only the 3-by-3 corner is missing, so you have to add 9 to complete it and then take 9 away to keep the value the same: x² + 6x = (x + 3)² − 9. Use the slider to change x; the shape and the numbers update to show the identity works for every x. Check the box to show or hide the missing corner.
